redCandidate.publicEntry: inspectTokenDiscipline() for the current project MCP configuration
redCandidate.setup: Use the checked-in project configuration, whose independent .mcp.json, .gemini/settings.json, and .codex/config.toml surfaces contain 4, 4, and 9 MCP servers respectively while the configured per-client budget is 10.

args: const assert = await import(`node:assert/strict`); const { inspectTokenDiscipline } = await import(`./scripts/lib/token-discipline/index.mjs`); const report = inspectTokenDiscipline({ rootDir: process.cwd(), projectRoot: process.cwd() }); assert.equal(report.enabledMcpServers, 9); assert.equal(report.warnings.some((warning) => warning.startsWith(`enabledMcpServers=`)), false);

redCandidate.expected: The public diagnostic reports 9, the largest active client configuration surface, and emits no aggregate MCP-budget warning.
redCandidate.observed: The command exits nonzero because the current public diagnostic sums independent surfaces to 17 before comparing with the budget.
redCandidate.failureReason: The inspector adds all candidate configuration counts even though those files describe different client runtimes rather than one simultaneously active MCP set.
